rationale: Ground truth has zero substantive concerns (bot hit a usage limit, human just said lgtm), so recall is trivially satisfied by both. Both candidates converge on the same genuinely valid, diff-grounded gap — tests mock out base() so the actual renamed-attribute regression is never exercised — and both back it with concrete file:line evidence and runnable test suggestions. X is better calibrated (explicit Approve verdict matching the real lgtm outcome, clearer separation of in-scope vs. follow-up items) while Y pads its output with five near-duplicate 'resolved' bullets restating the same pre-existing diffusion-mode caveat and includes a malformed '?:754' location tag, slightly hurting precision and actionability despite also offering nicely formatted GitHub suggestion blocks.
